title: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0
summary: Given a positive integer n, you can add or subtract any power of 2.
statement: Given a positive integer n, you can add or subtract any power of 2. Determine the least number of such operations needed to reduce n to 0. A number is considered a power of 2 if it equals 2 raised to the power of some non-negative integer i.
constraints: In one operation add or subtract any nonnegative power of two.
Keep intermediate integers nonnegative without loss of optimality.
Return the minimum operations reducing positive n to zero.
reference_solution:
def minimum_power_operations_to_zero(n):
    operations=0
    while n:
        lowest=n&-n
        if n& (lowest*2):n+=lowest
        else:n-=lowest
        operations+=1
    return operations

hints: The lowest set bit can either be subtracted away or added to create a carry.
For isolated ones, subtract; at the start of consecutive ones, adding once collapses the run through carrying.
Repeat on the new integer until it becomes zero.
This constructs the minimum-weight signed binary representation: each isolated bit costs one, while every run is optimally represented by its two boundaries.

tests.explanation: Subtracting 8, adding 1, then subtracting 32 reaches zero in three operations.
A shortest signed-power representation uses three operations.
